newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Berisha extends amnesty to rebels by a week.
newsitem.headline: Berisha extends amnesty to rebels by a week.

text.p: Albanian President Sali Berisha on Sunday extended by a week an amnesty for rebels who have seized control of most of the south of the country to hand in their weapons.

In a nationally broadcast address before resuming talks with political party leaders on ending the crisis in the country, Berisha also urged the formation of a national unity government including all parties to rule intil new elections within two months.

The call for a new government from all parties appeared to be a concession, since the right-wing Albanian leader has previously refused to include the ex-communist Socialists, the largest opposition party, in any interim administration.

Berisha was meeting party leaders as rebels in the south who are calling for his resignation were consolidating their hold over the region after seizing weapons from army depots and setting up road blocks.

"Within one week all those armed must surrender weapons and ammunition," Berisha said, a few hours after a 48-hour amnesty for the surrender of weapons expired. He made no explicit pledge not to resume military action against the insurgents.

Opposition politicians have been pressing Berisha for new elections organised by an interim non-party government, but argue they cannot be held while the country is under emergency rule imposed last week.
